2126345730121949193.en_summary: (Reposted by @JasonL_Capital) You could buy 100 shares of $SPCX right now for $13,129. Or you could buy the $130 call LEAP expiring January 2028 for $3,420. Leveraged exposure to 100 shares. 74% less capital. 420 days of runway. Strike: $130 Expiration: Jan 21, 2028 Premium: ~$34.20 per share ($3,420 per contract) Breakeven: $164.20 If $SPCX hits $175, this LEAP returns ~32% If $SPCX hits $200, this LEAP returns ~105% If $SPCX hits $250, this LEAP returns ~251% 100 shares at $250 would return ~90%. Why I like the setup: - Q3 revenue was $14.6B, up 161% year over year, and SpaceX swung to $4.4B of net income from a $1.1B loss - Starlink added 1.6M subscribers in the quarter to reach 13.6M, and connectivity revenue grew 69% - Super Intelligence, the AI compute and Grok segment, did $7.6B and is now the largest segment - Management guided Q1 2027 revenue to $33B-$37B - Starship reached orbit for the first time on Flight 14 and deployed 26 V3 Starlink satellites - The stock trades below its $135 IPO price and about 35% under its June closing high - 420 days gives the thesis time to play out The max you can lose on a LEAP is the entire premium you paid. In this case, that's $3,420 per contract. LEAPs are leveraged and can lose value quickly if the stock drops or stays flat. Only size this so you're comfortable losing all of it. Note: LEAPs are one tool inside a broader portfolio. Owning shares is always the primary use of capital. This is a selective add-on for high-conviction moments when conditions align. NFA DYOR
